 By
 Lesley Goldberg

 SHOW BUSINESS From left, HBO’s Lanterns , Netflix’s Bridgerton and Apple TV’s Pluribus . Courtesy of Warner Bros. Television/DC Studios/HBO, Liam Daniel/Netflix, Courtesy of Sony Pictures Television/High Bridge Productions/Bristol Circle Entertainment/Apple TV 
 I scooped Adults’ season three renewal and spoke to John Landgraf about FX strategy, and I wrote about the sleight of hand behind HBO’s buying spree and cuts coming to David Ellison’s $6.6 billion in sports rights .
 Hi, it’s me again — back for the third time in your inbox this week!
 After breaking some happy TV news about Adults , I’m back with a reminder of Hollywood’s harsh reality: even a hit isn’t safe during corporate shake-ups. After the ouster of DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran , HBO’s  Lanterns  faces an uncertain future despite strong reviews and 10.5 million viewers for its finale. I’ve got new reporting on why a second season remains a coin flip — and what the new DC regime means for the rest of its TV slate.
 I’m also digging into new numbers revealing that Netflix’s engagement problems go well beyond the sophomore slump. And why Apple TV’s  Pluribus  is bucking Hollywood’s push to get hit shows back on the air faster — by a lot.
 Let’s get to it.
